title: A Border for the Cipher
premise: Vesper Lockridge, a crash investigator haunted by the deaths of her family in row twelve, has spent three years hidden in a government safe house, guarding a cipher recovered from the wreckage that implicates a defense contractor in the disaster. When the safe house is listed for sale online — with interior photos revealing the cipher's hiding place — Vesper realizes someone inside the protection program sold her out. Racing to the summit where the evidence could be exposed, she must ally with the broker who found the listing, trading the cipher itself for the chance to survive and name the guilty. In the end, Vesper surrenders the secret publicly rather than privately, choosing truth over safety, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Ansel Yarrow is the pen name of a former aviation insurance adjuster who spent a decade reconstructing accidents no one wanted explained. They write from a coastal town where fog keeps its own secrets, and this is their third thriller.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Three years after the crash, Vesper works cold cases by day and replays flight data by night, unable to sleep past 3:14 a.m. — the moment of impact. A routine inspection of her safe house reveals nothing wrong, but the reader sees her checking the cipher's hiding spot twice. Emotional beat: grief worn as routine.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A colleague sends her a real estate link as a joke: her house, for sale, with forty-one photos — including one of the loose floorboard where the cipher lives. She calls her handler and gets voicemail. Emotional beat: the floor of her invisible life giving way.

chapters.title: Forty-One Photographs
chapters.summary: Vesper studies each photo like crash debris, cataloguing what they reveal: the angle suggests an interior shoot, not a drone. Someone stood in her kitchen. She packs a go-bag but can't leave without the cipher. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into method.

chapters.title: Handler Down
chapters.summary: Handler Marsh's POV. Marsh discovers his access logs show queries he never made and realizes the protection program has been penetrated from above. He burns his notes and drives toward Vesper, knowing he's being followed. Emotional beat: duty curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Broker
chapters.summary: Dane Ivers' POV. Dane, a property broker who unknowingly hosted the listing photographer, traces the commission to a shell company and finds Vesper waiting in his office with questions. He offers help; she offers suspicion. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Cipher Says
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, flashback-woven. We learn the cipher — recovered from row twelve's black box supplement — contains maintenance falsifications tied to Halcyon Dynamics, the contractor whose parts were on the plane. Vesper explains why she never released it: no one who knew it has survived. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Marsh Arrives Late
chapters.summary: Marsh reaches the safe house to find it staged for showing, agents sweeping it. He escapes with a burner phone and contacts Vesper through Dane. His warning: the leak goes to the directorate. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against institution.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The trio meets at a motel; Vesper tests Dane by feeding him false cipher details, which surface within hours on a dark-web forum. Confronted, Dane admits he was hired to find her — then flipped when he saw the listing's buyer. Emotional beat: betrayal repurposed into alliance.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Dane's POV. The shell company traces to Aldous Wren, Halcyon's founder, attending the same summit where oversight hearings convene in nine days. Dane realizes he wasn't hired to sell a house; he was hired to deliver a woman. Emotional beat: complicity dawning.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Planning chapter: they map the summit's security, press presence, and Wren's schedule. Vesper insists on going herself; Marsh argues for handing the cipher to federal prosecutors instead. First open fracture between love (Dane) and duty (Marsh). Emotional beat: the cost of choosing.

chapters.title: Photographs of Home
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude. Vesper and Dane inventory her life in boxes — photos of row twelve's funeral, her daughter's drawing taped inside a cabinet visible in listing photo thirty-three. Dane asks what she'll do when it's over; she can't imagine 'after.' Emotional beat: tenderness inside siege.

chapters.title: The Decoy Drop
chapters.summary: They feed a forged cipher location to the forum, staging a handoff that draws Wren's cleaners away from the real route. It half-works: the cleaners bite, but Marsh is photographed at the decoy. Emotional beat: victory with a bill attached.

chapters.title: Marsh Taken
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV, fragmented. Interrogated by men with federal badges and private payrolls, Marsh holds out until they show him Vesper's daughter's drawing — proof they've had deeper access than anyone knew. He gives them a partial truth to protect the rest. Emotional beat: sacrifice measured in pieces.

chapters.title: Partial Truths
chapters.summary: Vesper learns Marsh talked and assumes betrayal; Dane argues the partial key they now hold proves Marsh gave them only the decoy layer. Trust between Vesper and Dane strains over whether to abort. Emotional beat: love interrogating itself.

chapters.title: Wren's Offer
chapters.summary: A message reaches Vesper through old program channels: Wren offers full immunity, a new identity, and restoration of her family's sealed crash report — in exchange for the cipher, quietly, before the summit. He includes a photo proving he knows about row twelve's true cause already. Emotional beat: survival priced in silence.

chapters.title: The Night She Almost Slept
chapters.summary: Vesper weighs the offer and, for the first time in three years, sleeps — exhausted into surrender, dreaming of row twelve. She wakes certain: Wren doesn't want the cipher destroyed; he wants it owned. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Breaking the Program
chapters.summary: They extract Marsh using the decoy network still live, discovering his captors kept him near the summit site — arrogance as vulnerability. Marsh, freed, confirms the directorate leak and brings the program's own evidence chain. Emotional beat: the institution's debt coming due.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Allies positioned: Dane inside as venue staff, Marsh working federal contacts, Vesper carrying the cipher under accreditation borrowed from a dead investigator's file. Wren's cleaners sweep the perimeter. Everything converges tomorrow. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Wren's people intercept Vesper in the service corridor; the exchange turns violent when she hands over a device that wipes itself. Dane takes a bullet meant for her; Marsh triggers the federal response he's spent days arranging. Emotional beat: love paying duty's toll.

chapters.title: What She Gave Away
chapters.summary: Vesper, cornered and bleeding beside Dane, makes her choice: she broadcasts the cipher's contents to every press terminal at the summit rather than trade it privately. Wren's arrest unfolds on screens above the hall. Emotional beat: the secret detonating into daylight.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Hearings begin; the protection program is dismantled; Marsh testifies. Dane recovers slowly, and Vesper stays — the first time she's chosen to stay anywhere since row twelve. The house sells to strangers who will never know what lived beneath the floorboard. Emotional beat: exhale.

chapters.title: Through the Night
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Vesper's POV. Months later, at a memorial for the passengers, Vesper reads row twelve's names aloud without her voice breaking. That night she sleeps until morning. The last image: dawn light on an empty bedside table where the cipher used to be. Emotional beat: survival's price paid, and worth it.
